items.title: Exclusivity Lite? Everyday Brands Help Sell Near-Premium Credit Cards
items.summary: With annual fees for luxury credit cards reaching stratospheric heights, issuers are pursuing the next level down in affluence with more modestly priced alternatives.  “What has emerged is what I would call the upper-middle-class option,” principal consumer finance analyst Ted Rossman tells The Wall Street Journal’s Ben Glickman and Jasmine Li.  American Express  hiked the fee on its Platinum card by $200 last year to $895, but its Gold card costs only $325.
